thread.title: Apple Stock Falls As Investor Warns About China Threat | Investor's Business Daily

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Apple Stock Falls As Investor Warns About China Threat | Investor's Business Daily
text:
Apple stock fell Friday after hedge fund billionaire David Einhorn said he sold his Apple ( AAPL ) stake in part over fears that the iPhone maker will be impacted by growing U.S.-China trade tensions.
X Einhorn's firm, Greenlight Capital, sold its remaining Apple stock on valuation concerns and his fear of Chinese retaliation to U.S. tariffs, according to his third-quarter letter to investors, CNBC reported . Greenlight Capital slashed its stake in Apple in the second quarter.
"We ultimately sold because our differentiated thesis from 2011 has become consensus," Einhorn said. "We are somewhat worried about Chinese retaliation against America's trade policies."
Greenlight said its investment in Apple had earned its clients over $1 billion since its first purchase of the stock in May 2010.

Apple stock notched an all-time high of 233.47 on Wednesday. For the year, it is up 33% in value.
Lately Apple shares have been riding high on reports that the company's iPhone XS and XS Max handsets are selling better than last year's models.
Next up is the iPhone XR, a midrange handset with a 6.1-inch LCD screen and a range of colored cases. Apple will start taking preorders for the iPhone XR on Oct. 19, with sales beginning a week later.
